rationale: Evidence from iteration 4 (score 663.5, best so far): the oval is solved (20/20 finished, max_error 0.021, about 1.8 s). The s-bend finishes 19/20 (0.95). The slalom still fails 20/20 by off_track at progress 0.32, with max_error about 0.064 (just over the 0.06 m limit), 0.4 line-loss events per run, and low steering oscillation (0.31). Moving the sensors forward and widening the array (iteration 4) moved slalom progress only from 0.31 to 0.32, so sensing reach and lead are no longer the main limit. The robot is jittering very little, so the failure is slow steering authority on fast alternating bends, which is the hypothesis (a) recorded in iteration 4. Change: raise kp from 2.6 to 3.0 (about 15%) for a stronger correction per unit of signal. Raise kd from 0.9 to 1.1 so damping keeps pace with the larger proportional gain; oscillation has margin (0.31 against the rough ceiling of about 0.5 flagged in earlier hypotheses). Geometry is unchanged from iteration 4 (seven sensors at y=0.07, x from -0.08 to +0.08, weights x/0.04, wheel_track 0.10, mass 0.6), and base_speed stays at 1.0 so the oval and s-bend finish time is not affected and the stall or timeout risk does not rise. Expected result: slalom max_error drops toward 0.05 to 0.055 and slalom progress rises above 0.5 with fewer off-track ends; s-bend finish rate holds at or above 0.95; oval stays near 950. Hypotheses to check next: (a) if slalom still ends off track with max_error near 0.06 and oscillation stays under 0.4, steering authority is still limiting, so try kp near 3.4 or a narrower wheel_track of 0.09; (b) if oscillation rises above 0.5 on the s-bend, kd needs to rise further relative to kp; (c) if the robot finishes reliably with completion_time above 2.5 s, raise base_speed toward 1.2.
